content_units: Based on your priorities,   Program A is the better value pick   if your main goals are   lower cost   and   finishing faster   while working full-time.
Program B is the better balance pick   if you care more about   career support, flexibility, and portfolio-ready applied work  .
-   Best for affordability + speed:     Program A
-   Best for full-time job compatibility + applied/business portfolio:     Program B
-   Overall recommendation:     Program B  , unless minimizing cost is your clear  1 priority
Criteria   Weight   Program A   Program B
- Program B:   24 months  , which still fits but leaves no buffer
- Program A: strong statistics core suggests rigor, but less evidence of applied showcase work
- Program B: stronger business analytics and electives more likely to produce practical project outputs
- Program B:   10–12 hrs/week  ,   fully online  , better for schedule stability
Option 1: Program A   Best on cost and speed   Lowest tuition
- Stronger fit if you want a more technical/statistical foundation
- Main downside: weaker career support and less flexibility because of residencies
Option 2: Program B   Best for work-life fit and applied outcomes   Stronger flexibility
- Lower weekly workload makes it easier to sustain alongside a full-time job
- Fully online format removes travel/logistics friction
- Stronger business analytics and electives likely support more employer-facing portfolio work
- Active career coaching directly addresses your practical outcomes after graduation
If your priorities are ranked exactly as stated:
Then   Program A narrowly wins on a strict weighted matrix  .

But if you want the option that is more sustainable while employed and more likely to generate career-ready deliverables,   Program B is the smarter real-world choice  . The difference in score is small, and Program B’s strengths line up better with:
To make the matrix concrete, I treated:
-   “Practical portfolio projects”   as favoring applied analytics, business analytics, electives, and coaching support
-   “Keeping a full-time job”   as favoring lower weekly workload, no travel, and fully online delivery
-   “Within 2 years”   as a pass for both, with extra credit to the shorter program
headings: Option 1: Program A | Best on cost and speed | Lowest tuition
Option 2: Program B | Best for work-life fit and applied outcomes | Stronger flexibility
